acceptance: The public generation request accepts or derives an explicit seed and records the seed plus generation-algorithm version in output metadata.
Each logical record or fixed logical partition receives deterministic random input independent of worker count, task completion order, and process scheduling.
Serial and parallel generation use the same deterministic algorithm and produce byte-identical normalized output for the same inputs, seed, and algorithm version.
Tests compare worker counts 1, 2, several, and greater than logical partition count; repeated runs and reordered task completion produce identical results.
A different seed produces a demonstrably different dataset, while legacy callers receive a documented compatibility default.
No implementation uses module-global random.seed or shares a mutable RNG across workers.
context: Worker-count invariance is the required property. Per-chunk RNG instances are insufficient if chunk boundaries themselves change with max_workers.
description:
TPC-DI parallel data generation partitions input according to max_workers and uses random generation inside those partitions. Reproducibility must not depend on how many workers happen to be available. Define a seed and logical-record partition contract shared by serial and parallel execution.

Decision boundary: derive randomness from stable logical identities or fixed logical partitions, not scheduling order or worker/chunk boundaries. Do not seed or mutate Python's process-global random generator.
